title: Scotch Eggs
subtitle: Soft-boiled egg wrapped in seasoned sausagemeat and fried
excerpt: A soft-boiled egg wrapped in well-seasoned sausagemeat, coated in crispy breadcrumbs and deep-fried until golden. The yolk should be jammy rather than hard-boiled. A pub classic turned weekend project.

recipe.sourceNotes: Scotch eggs are believed to have been invented by the London department store Fortnum and Mason around 1738, originally sold as a travelling food. They became a staple of British pub lunches and picnics throughout the twentieth century. The traditional version has a fully hard-boiled egg; the modern preference since the 2010s pub food revival is for a soft, jammy yolk, achieved by a shorter boiling time before wrapping.

recipeTools.notes: For boiling the eggs and for deep frying.

content.text: Timing the initial boil is critical for a jammy yolk: 6 minutes from boiling for a medium egg gives a set white and a yolk that is still soft at the centre. Cool in cold water immediately to stop cooking. The sausagemeat layer should be even and not too thin or the egg will push through when frying. Fry at 170 C so the meat cooks through and the breadcrumbs colour before the outside burns.
Lower the 4 eggs into boiling water. Boil for exactly 6 minutes. Remove and cool immediately in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes. Peel carefully and set aside.

Mix the sausagemeat with the mustard, parsley, salt, and pepper. Divide into 4 equal portions. Flatten each portion into a thin disc. Dust a peeled egg in flour, place in the centre of a disc, and wrap the sausagemeat evenly around it, pressing the seams closed.
Set up three bowls: flour, beaten egg, and panko breadcrumbs. Roll each sausagemeat-wrapped egg in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs. Press the crumbs firmly.
Heat the oil to 170 C in a deep pan. Fry 2 eggs at a time for 7 to 8 minutes, turning, until deep golden all over. Drain on kitchen paper. Rest for 5 minutes before cutting in half.
